name: MoNuSeg APGCC 30/7/14 split
description: Reproducible train/val/test split for MoNuSeg 2018 used by the APGCC counting baseline. train+val come from 'MoNuSeg 2018 Training Data' (37 images); test is the official 'MoNuSegTestData' (14 images). Anyone using this file gets exactly the same image-level split.

rationale.paper_reference: Kumar et al., 'A Dataset and a Technique for Generalized Nuclear Segmentation for Computational Pathology', IEEE TMI 2017 (the original MoNuSeg dataset paper).
rationale.paper_protocol_note: The paper's own protocol is 12 train / 4 val / 14 test over 30 images (Table I + Sec.V). We do NOT copy it verbatim, because the 37-image MoNuSeg-2018 training set is NOT a superset of the paper's exact 30 images (organ composition differs: paper has 6 liver / no lung-brain-cervix; the 37-set has 1 liver, 6 lung, 1 brain, 1 cervix). So 'extract the paper's 30 from the 37' is not literally possible.
rationale.split_policy: 30 train / 7 val / 14 test. Validation = the 7 images from the rarest / most peripheral organs in the training pool (held-out-organ style, matching the paper's 'different-organ test' generalization philosophy). The remaining 30 train; the official 14 test are untouched.
rationale.organ_source: Organ per image derived from the TCGA Tissue Source Site (TSS) code (2nd barcode field) via the authoritative GDC TSS code table.
caveats: Brain and Colon appear in val (not train) but also appear in the test set -> the model never trains on brain/colon. This is intentional (generalization to unseen organs), but expect weaker test performance on those two organs.
val organs (liver/stomach/cervix) are absent from the test set, so the validation metric is only a partial proxy for test performance.
